source.stem:
A ball is dropped from a table-top. Air resistance may be ignored.
Which row describes the velocity and the acceleration of the ball at point X?

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: friction is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: Use this when two surfaces are in contact while an object slides or rolls.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: friction -> opposition to motion -> object slows or stops happens first, and that produces surface contact and irregularities.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when Use this when two surfaces are in contact while an object slides or rolls is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: Friction acts between surfaces in contact and opposes the motion of the object; it arises due to irregularities in the two surfaces, and it is greater on rough surfaces. surface contact and irregularities -> friction -> opposition to motion -> object slows or stops The learner correctly applies this rule: Friction acts between surfaces in contact and opposes the motion of the object; it arises due to irregularities in the two surfaces, and it is greater on rough surfaces. Friction appears only after the object has already stopped, so it does not oppose motion while the object moves.
